Whether the existing natural gas production, pipelines between states and underground storage (store, injection and withdrawal) may retire. They are then optimised between zero and their existing capacity, so assets whose fixed O&M outweighs their value retire; their sunk investment is not counted. Retrofitting to hydrogen (``retrofit``) does not need it: without it, the existing capacity is kept, as natural gas or retrofitted. Whenever a storage retires or is retrofitted, its withdrawal keeps the share of its existing capacity that its store keeps, and its injection at least that share and at most its withdrawal. Trade pipelines and linepack stay fixed.

Natural gas infrastructure retrofitted to hydrogen in the first investment period, with the hydrogen sector (``E-G-H``). The model optimizes how much of the existing capacity to retrofit, from zero to all. What is retrofitted is taken from the natural gas capacity: the gas left plus the hydrogen capacity over its conversion factor is the existing gas capacity, or at most it if it may also retire (``economic_retirement``). See :ref:`data-hydrogen`.
